practices.name: Candle petition
how: This is not lighting a candle. It's giving an intention a physical body — a flame that keeps working after your attention moves on. Pray first, always: the prayer is the authority under the petition, and without it you're just burning wax. Speak to God plainly about what you're asking for and why it's already yours to ask.

Then write the petition on clean paper, present tense, as if it has already arrived — not 'let me get the contract' but 'the contract is signed and the money is in my account.' Fold the paper toward you to draw in; away from you to release. Dress the candle with the oil that matches the work — prosperity oil for money, visibility oil for being seen — stroking toward you for drawing work.

Set the paper under the candle, light it, and say what you wrote once, out loud, with the voice you'd use for something true. Let it burn down in one sitting when you can; a snuffed candle can be relit, a blown-out one argues with the ask. When doubt shows up while the flame is working — and it will — you don't re-petition. One petition, full trust. The wax holds it so you don't have to.

practices.name: Intention setting
how: Intention setting on a New Moon isn't a wish list — it's a planting. You're deciding what version of your life gets your agreement for the next cycle. Do it after the exact New Moon moment, not before; the dark moon is for emptying, the first hours after are for seeding.

Sit somewhere quiet, pray first to anchor it, then write no more than three intentions — present tense, first person, specific enough that you'd recognize their arrival. 'I am paid what I ask' plants. 'I want more money' scatters. Feel each one in the body as you write it: if your chest tightens, that intention has a block attached — write it anyway and note the tightness. That's information for the somatic work, not a reason to shrink the ask.

Then leave them alone. You don't re-read intentions daily or check on the seed. You act normal, as Neville says — you live as the woman who wrote them and already knows. Revisit only at the Full Moon, to notice what's sprouting.

practices.name: SATS
how: SATS — the State Akin To Sleep — is Neville Goddard's most direct line into the subconscious, and you have access to it every single night. In the drowsy state just before sleep, the gatekeeper between conscious and subconscious mind steps aside. What you impress there, feeling it as real, the deeper mind accepts as instruction.

In bed, body heavy, eyes closed: build one small scene that would only exist if the wish were already fulfilled. Not the whole movie — one moment. The phone in your hand as you read the email that says yes. The weight of the pen signing the engagement letter. Make it sensory: temperature, texture, the sound in the room. Then loop that single scene, slowly, letting the feeling of it being done settle into your chest — satisfaction, not longing. Longing tells the subconscious it hasn't happened; satisfaction tells it that it has.

If you fall asleep inside the scene, perfect — that's the aim, not a failure. If the 'is this working' voice shows up, don't argue with it; return to the scene the way you'd return to the breath in meditation. The proof isn't the feeling that night. It's the bridge of incidents that starts building in the days after — and your only job then is to not dig up the seed.

practices.name: Scovel Shinn decree
how: Florence Scovel Shinn taught that the spoken word is architecture — 'your word is your wand.' A decree is not an affirmation you repeat two hundred times hoping to believe it. It's a legal declaration, spoken once or twice with full authority, that names what is yours by divine right and dissolves what stands in the way.

Stand or sit upright. Say it out loud — the voice matters; a decree whispered apologetically decrees apology. The classic structure: name what is yours by divine right, release how it arrives, and refuse the counterfeit. Hers for you might sound like: 'Infinite Spirit, open the way for my right work, under grace, in a perfect way. The consulting that is mine by divine right comes to me easily; what is not mine falls away without loss. I give thanks that it is already done.'

'Under grace, in a perfect way' is the release valve — it hands the how back to God so you don't strangle the outcome with strategy. Decree it, then act as if the papers are already being drawn up. When fear speaks later in the day, you don't re-decree in panic; you say 'I have spoken' and let the word work.

practices.name: Hand-on-heart
how: This is nervous system work disguised as a gesture. Your body learned somewhere that having more — money, visibility, love — isn't safe, and no amount of mindset work overrides a body that's braced. This practice speaks to the body in the only language it trusts: touch, breath, and repetition.

Place your whole hand flat on your chest, real contact, real warmth. Take two slow breaths where the exhale is longer than the inhale — that's the switch that tells the vagus nerve the threat is over. Then say the week's phrase out loud, low and unhurried: 'It's safe to have more,' or 'It's safe to be chosen.' Then — this is the actual practice — notice what the body does with it. The tight jaw, the shallow catch in the breath, the flicker of 'no it isn't.' You're not fighting that response. You're witnessing it while staying in contact, which is how the body learns the sentence and safety can coexist.

Thirty seconds, done before the trigger, not after — before you open email, before you say the rate, before the date. The resistance getting quieter over weeks is the metric. This is the ground floor of every other practice you do: a regulated body is the receiving apparatus.
